text:
max: Quick check — canary runs from this morning show KV cache hit rate dropping ~12% after ~18k requests. Not sure if it's eviction policy or fragmentation. Anyone else seeing this?

priya: Saw that too. Pattern looks like many small prefixes piling up, pushing out larger useful entries.

max: I'll attach a quick flame / profile but wanted to coordinate before running the heavy bench again. perf-bot: ran nightly, tag `canary-2025-10-18`.

perf-bot: nightly-bench results: <https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/bench/2025/10/18/kv-canary> (summary: avg latency +9ms, kv-hit 78% -> 66%) :warning:

dave: tagging memory fragmentation — are we still using the same slab allocator config? Could be fragmentation from mixed sizes.

anna: Can you paste the profile? I can run jemalloc stats on the canary machines. Also curious about prefix length distribution in the workload.

max: here's the minimal repro I ran locally:

```
// simulate workload: 70% short prefixes < 64b, 30% long prefixes 256-1024b
for i in 0..18000 {
  let k = if rand() < 0.7 { short_prefix() } else { long_prefix() };
  cache.set(k, value_of_size(rand_range(128, 8192)));
  if i % 100 == 0 { send_requests_matching_short_prefixes(); }
}
```

priya: Thanks. My hypothesis: prefix cache's LRU is size-agnostic so many small keys evict large cached KV entries that serve many requests -> hit rate drop. We tried a size-aware LRU in an old branch (refs: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1298>) but reverted due to tail latency spikes.

dave: Right — advocate for a weighted-LRU (weight = entry_size * frequency_estimate). We need to test tradeoff between hit-rate and tail P99.

anna: I'll run two benches: current, and weighted-lru with a simple weight=length prototype. Can run on canary-srv-03. Need the exact workload profile — max can you export the request histogram?

max: exporting now. payload: 73% queries hit /embed/prefix, avg seq len 320, request QPS ~240 in canary (bursts). Export: `s3://redwood-internal/tmp/kv-workload-2025-10-18.json`

priya: Also check KV compaction/gc intervals — if tiny entries create many small allocations, compaction frequency might matter. We had a change last month that reduced compaction to avoid CPU churn.

anna: Good point. I'll run with current compaction and with aggressive compaction. Running two benches in parallel, about ~30m each. Will post links when done.

perf-bot: job started: bench-weighted-lru-2025-10-18 (canary-srv-03). ETA ~28m.

dave: If weighted-LRU helps hit-rate, consider a fast-path for small entries: keep a dedicated small-entry slab that is GCed less aggressively. That avoids evicting large multi-use entries.

max: For tracking: can we add a Prometheus histogram for "kv_prefix_fragmentation_ratio"? Right now we only have hit/miss counters. Need a metric for average contiguous memory per prefix bucket.

priya: +1. That will help alerting too. I'll open a tiny PR to add the gauge and a Grafana panel.

anna: Bench complete (weighted-lru): avg hit-rate 82% (current 66%), avg latency +4ms but P99 unchanged. Link: <https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/bench/2025/10/18/weighted-lru>.

max: Nice. Can you also run the aggressive-compaction test?

anna: Aggressive compaction runs next. perf-bot: job started: bench-aggressive-compaction-2025-10-18.

perf-bot: bench-aggressive-compaction finished: hit-rate 68%, latency +12ms, memory pressure reduced by ~6%. Link: <https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/bench/2025/10/18/aggressive_compaction>.

dave: So weighted-LRU looks promising — better hit-rate and not much P99 impact. Aggressive compaction helps memory but hurts latency. Tradeoffs clear.

priya: I'll prep a proposal: enable weighted-LRU behind a feature flag, add metric `kv_prefix_fragmentation_ratio`, and keep compaction conservative. Will include rollback plan.

max: Thanks team. @anna can you share perf artifacts (heap profiles + jemalloc stats) so I can dig deeper into fragmentation?

anna: Uploaded `/artifacts/kv/2025-10-18/weighted-lru/heap.profile` and `jemalloc.stat` to the bench page.

max: Great. I'll start an RFC for gradual rollout and add observability queries. If anyone wants to review the PR, ping me. :thumbsup:
